# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-11 (Extended v101)

## Setting and Time
Multiple periods spanning French Revolution to 1826. **Current narrative point (Autumn Year 3, dual settings)**: (1) Paris, le Petit-Picpus convent district—Valjean and Cosette in sanctuary; M. Gillenormand's residences (Rue Férou, Rue des Filles-du-Calvaire); (2) English provincial harbor towns (Dunstead, Yarlby, Kelford, Staveford, Ravenmere, Ostcombe, Gulhaven, Kelmere, Dunby, Dungate, Torton); Vernon (Colonel Pontmercy's residence). **Environmental conditions (Autumn Year 3)**: children chased hoops down lanes; frost silvered hedges overnight; wind came off water with salt/tar smell; roads rutted and puddled after thaw; light went early; smoke lay flat over fields.

## Primary Locations

**PARIS - LE PETIT-PICPUS DISTRICT**: Between Faubourg Saint-Antoine and la Râpée; Number 62 Rue Petit-Picpus (convent carriage gate). **Convent complex**: Great Convent (Bernardines-Benedictines nuns), Boarding-school, Little Convent (aged nuns). **Interior garden**: Vast oblong with poplar alley, forest trees, gnarled fruit-tree, vegetable beds, melon patch, old well, stone benches. **Chapel**: Window visible from garden. **Burial location**: Mother Crucifixion's vault beneath grand altar. **Vaugirard cemetery**: Ancient burial ground with Prefecture Permission for nightfall interments; former grave-digger Father Mestienne (deceased); replaced by "little Father Lenoir."

**M. GILLENORMAND'S RESIDENCES**: **Rue Férou house** (frequented Madame de T.'s salon twice weekly from 1817 onward)—Madame la Baronne de T., worthy respectable Royalist, salon twice-weekly, tea, royalist politics. **Newly established Rue des Filles-du-Calvaire in the Marais** (after conclusion of Marius's classical studies). Doors closed during day; opens evenings after five o'clock dinner.

**VERNON**: Colonel Pontmercy's residence. **Colonel's grave**: Vaugirard cemetery; black wooden cross with white letters "COLONEL BARON PONTMERCY."

**SAINT-SULPICE CHAPEL**: Location where Marius knelt upon chair inscribed "Monsieur Mabeuf, warden"; Church-warden Mabeuf introduced himself to Marius here.

**QUAI DES ORFÉVRES (Paris)**: Location of engraver where Marius ordered hundred cards bearing name "Le Baron Marius Pontmercy."

**GORBEAU HOVEL (50-52)**: Salpêtrière district, outskirts Paris. Posted "Chambers to let"; inhabited by indigent individuals. **Current tenant—Jondrette family**: Father hired chamber; instructed portress to respond affirmatively if inquired for Pole, Italian, or Spaniard.

**ENGLISH PROVINCIAL SETTINGS**: Dunstead, Yarlby, Kelford, Staveford, Ravenmere, Ostcombe, Gulhaven, Kelmere, Dunby, Dungate, Torton; market towns with parsonages, forges, granaries, ovens, wells, lanes. **Population movements**: Yera Haskick left Dunstead for Kelmere; Rinelle quit Kelford for Torton; Kadrek Brackick followed to Torton; Lurald Stenworth told Thizek Stenenridge deed to Kelmere pastures forged; Luena packed trunk, moved Staveford to Dungate; Rozek Stenenridge followed within month; Volan Stenworth (now Peten) mended sleeve by window, said little. **New births (Dunstead)**: Son Ferald Stenworth and daughter Isvie Stenworth born to Luwyn Brackick, father Lurald Stenworth. **Rumor (Dunstead)**: Ismira claimed Wenelle Lindmere drowned crossing estuary (no body seen); Ismira told Luena granary fire was set on purpose (claim/rumor). **Other individuals**: Yewyn Haskick (sorts old letters by candlelight); Yewyn and Tatho Brackick (discuss weather, harvest, lame horse); Tatho complains of aching back; Elra Corrford (watches clouds, predicted rain wrongly); Fenelle Lindmere (hummed childhood tune, burned letter from Yedan Corrford revealing Stenson family once owed blood debt to Stenenridge family); Lura (sorts old letters by candlelight); Kassa and Lurald Stenworth (remark on river level); Parcel from Tatho reached Marald with amber map; In Ostcombe: Bossuet directing steps toward lawyer profession, pursuing law studies after Bahorel's manner, lodges with various people including Joly; Joly studying medicine, two years younger than Bossuet.

## Jean Valjean's Development

**CURRENT STATUS (Autumn Year 3)**: Integrated into convent life as assistant gardener; inhabits old garden hut with Fauchelevent. Works daily; pruner of trees; budded ungrafted orchard trees. **Spiritual transformation**: Meditations on grace; blood ran cold at grateful nuns' songs—realized he justly chastified while wretch shook fist at God. Scaled wall made to escape other expiation now served entrance to sanctuary. Pride vanished; scrutinized heart; wept. All recent months led back to Bishop's holy injunctions—Cosette through love, convent through humility. Knelt in garden walks at eventide; prostrated in prayer. Soul became compounded of silence, perfume, simplicity, joy. Two houses of God received him critically: first when society rejected; second when society pursued.

## Cosette's Development

**INITIAL STATE**: Knew nothing; could say nothing. Unhappiness trained silence. Hardly regained confidence with Valjean. **Convent integration**: Speedily accustomed; regretted Catherine but dared not say. Told Valjean: "Father, if I had known, I would have brought her away." Thinks herself his daughter. Became convent scholar; received pupil garb. Valjean restored mourning suit from Thénardier departure; locked up garments plus stockings/shoes with camphor/aromatics in valise on chair near bed; always carried key. Cosette asked: "Father, what is there in that box which smells so good?" At appointed hour flies to hut filling it with paradise; adored him because sisters melancholy and he kind.

## Fauchelevent's Role

**Identity**: Old crippled gardener admitted approximately two years previously on Valjean's (Mayor Madeleine's) recommendation after cart accident. Limps; takes nearly quarter hour traversing short distances; complains aching back. **Execution of concealment**: Used service door placing Cosette in vintage basket with deaf fruit-seller (Rue Chemin-Vert). Placed Valjean in coffin; transported in hearse to Vaugirard cemetery. Grave-digger Father Mestienne dead; replaced by "little Father Lenoir" (jug red wine). Fauchelevent found lost card, buried corpse, filled grave himself. **Character**: Grateful, talkative, excitable; calls Valjean "Father Madeleine"; peasant of Picardy. Perceived generous action as dying man perceives good wine. Air of convent destroyed personal selfishness; rendered good action absolutely necessary. **Current status**: Lives in garden hut with Valjean; continues gardening; sole person aware of full presence; only known ally/protector. Nuns do not suspect him; eyes fixed on God do not spy.

## Javert's Pursuit

**Reassignment and investigation**: Attached to Paris police after Valjean's escape (January 1823). Newspaper announced Valjean's death (December 1823); Javert remarked "That's a good entry." Police report concerning child abduction in Montfermeil revived memory; suspected Valjean sought daughter. **Secret investigation**: Without telling anyone, took coach to Montfermeil; followed mysterious lodger to Gorbeau house; hired room, listened at lodger's door; Valjean foiled spy by silence. Reasons for secrecy: (1) Indiscretion might alert Valjean; (2) Recapturing ex-convict reputed dead magnificent success; (3) Javert had taste for unforeseen. **Pursuit escalation**: Old woman warned Javert lodger intended to leave; Javert waited behind trees with two men at night. **Escape from Mouffetard**: Valjean cut street lantern rope; Javert found disorder, led astray. Followed from tree to tree; did not arrest hastily. **Current status (Autumn Year 3)**: Established sentinels, organized traps and ambuscades; sure convict could not be far off.

## Marius Pontmercy: Complete Development

**PARENTAGE AND EARLY YEARS**: Son of Colonel Pontmercy (chief of squadron, meagre half-pay); mother Madame Pontmercy (née Gillenormand, youngest daughter—"admirable woman in every sense"). Mother died 1815, leaving child. Colonel lives alone at Vernon.

**EARLY EDUCATION AND ESTRANGEMENT (Age 7)**: Grandfather kept no relations with son-in-law (colonel "a bandit" to him); colonel called "brigand of the Loire." Expressly agreed: Pontmercy never attempt to see or speak to son under penalty of disinheritance. **Secret paternal visits**: Colonel slipped away every two or three months, came to Paris secretly, posted himself at Saint-Sulpice at hour when Aunt Gillenormand led Marius to mass. Trembling lest aunt turn round, concealed behind pillar, motionless, not daring breathe, gazed at child. **Correspondence**: Twice yearly, Marius wrote duty letters dictated by aunt. Father answered with tender letters grandfather thrust into pocket unread.

**CLASSICAL STUDIES AND TRANSFORMATION**: Conclusion coincided with M. Gillenormand's departure from society. Old man established himself in Marais, Rue des Filles-du-Calvaire. **Summons to Vernon**: Marius seized with trembling fit upon notification to see father. Believed father did not love him. **Journey and Colonel's Death**: Diligence from Rue du Bouloi took trip by night, passed through Vernon. On very evening of Marius's arrival, colonel had attack of delirium; rose from bed crying: "My son is not coming! I shall go to meet him!" Ran out, fell prostrate on floor of antechamber. Had just expired. **Marius's first sight of father**: Gazed upon venerable and manly face, open eyes which saw not, white locks, robust limbs marked by sword-thrusts (brown lines) and bullet-holes (red stars). Felt ashamed and embarrassed at his own attitude; held hat in hand; dropped it on floor.

**PATERNAL LEGACY AND DOCUMENT**: Colonel left written instruction: "_For my son_.—The Emperor made me a Baron on the battle-field of Waterloo...my son shall take it and bear it." Below, the colonel added: "At that same battle of Waterloo, a sergeant saved my life. The man's name was Thénardier. I think he has recently been keeping a little inn, in a village in the neighborhood of Paris, at Chelles or Montfermeil. If my son meets him, he will do all the good he can to Thénardier." **Lost document (critical loss)**: While carrying Marius's duds to his chamber, Nicolette inadvertently let fall on attic staircase the medallion of black shagreen containing colonel's paper. Neither paper nor case found afterward. Marius convinced M. Gillenormand flung "his father's testament" in fire. He knew by heart few lines; paper and writing—that sacred relic—was his very heart.

**INTELLECTUAL AND POLITICAL TRANSFORMATION**: Preserved religious habits of childhood. One Sunday heard mass at Saint-Sulpice. Church-warden Mabeuf presented himself, told him about colonel's retreat, flowers, solitude. Marius came to full knowledge of that rare, sweet, sublime man, that lion-lamb which was his father. **Reading and Napoleon Conversion**: Read _Moniteur_, all histories of Republic and Empire, _Memorial de Sainte-Hélène_, all memoirs, newspapers, bulletins; devoured everything. First time encountered father's name in bulletins of grand army, had fever for week. From infancy imbued with party of 1814 judgments on Bonaparte; execrated him even more than Robespierre. On reading history, veil concealing Napoleon gradually rent. Each day saw more distinctly; one night alone in little chamber near roof, reading bulletins of grand army, beheld his father's name interspersed with Emperor's name; felt flood swelling and rising within him; thought he heard drums, cannon, trumpets, measured tread of battalions. Heart contracted; exclaimed: "Long live the Emperor!" **Metamorphosis**: From that moment, all was over. Ogre of Corsica, usurper, tyrant—all vanished, gave place to pale marble phantom of Cæsar. Emperor became something more for Marius: predestined constructor of French group. Fanaticism for sword took possession; complicated enthusiasm for idea. **Violent sort of good faith which took everything in lump**.

**ORDERED CARDS**: Became thoroughly revolutionist, profoundly democratic and republican; went to engraver on Quai des Orfévres and ordered hundred cards bearing name: _Le Baron Marius Pontmercy_.

**ESTRANGEMENT FROM GRANDFATHER**: By natural consequence, receded from grandfather in proportion as drew nearer to father and colonel's memory. Nothing betrayed on exterior. Only grew colder and colder; laconic at meals, rare in house. M. Gillenormand's diagnosis: "In love! I know all about it."

**QUEST FOR THÉNARDIER**: On one of brief trips, went to Montfermeil to obey injunction father left—sought old sergeant to Waterloo, inn-keeper Thénardier. Thénardier had failed, inn closed, no one knew what became of him. Marius away from house four days on this quest.

**RECENT CONFRONTATION AND VIOLENT QUARREL (Autumn Year 3)**: Marius returned from Vernon third day, descended at grandfather's door. Had thrown off travelling-coat and black ribbon. M. Gillenormand held one of Marius's cards in hand. Marius retorted with downcast eyes and severe air: "My father was a humble and heroic man, who served the Republic and France gloriously, who was great in the greatest history that men have ever made...who died forgotten and abandoned, and who never committed but one mistake, which was to love too fondly two ingrates, his country and myself." M. Gillenormand sprang to feet; every word produced effect of puffs of air from forge upon blazing brand. Cried: "Marius! Abominable child! I do not know what your father was! But what I do know is, that there never was anything but scoundrels among those men!...All who served B-u-o-naparté were brigands!...All cowards who fled before the Prussians and the English at Waterloo!" **Marius's anguish**: Quivered in every limb; like priest beholding sacred wafers cast to winds. Impossible for him to insult grandfather yet equally impossible for him to leave father unavenged. **Old man's response**: Turned whiter than his hair. Wheeled round towards bust of M. le Duc de Berry on chimney-piece, made profound bow. Then paced twice, slowly and in silence, from fireplace to window and from window to fireplace, making polished floor creak as though stone statue walking. **Marius's departure**: Went forth in indignation.

## M. Gillenormand and His World

**IDENTITY AND CHARACTER**: Worthy bourgeois; "consideration of absolutely first-rate quality"; dignified, honest, lofty in bourgeois fashion; great age added venerable dishevelment. **Two daughters**: Born ten years apart. **Youngest** (Marius's mother): Charming soul turned towards light, ethereal; died 1815. **Eldest** (Mademoiselle Gillenormand): Over forty, looked fifty; antique virtue, incombustible prude. Household of old man and old spinster touching aspect of two weaknesses leaning for support. **Servants**: Chambermaid Nicolette; short-breathed pursy Basque; porter.

**LIEUTENANT THÉODULE GILLENORMAND**: Great-grand-nephew on paternal side; led garrison life, outside family. Had "lady's waist," victorious manner of trailing sword and twirling moustache. Visited Paris very rarely; Marius had never seen him. **Favorite of Aunt Gillenormand** because she did not see him; not seeing people permits attributing all possible perfections. **Recent visit (Autumn Year 3)**: Théodule entered aunt's chamber while she worked on embroidery of Empire and Restoration to distract herself from curiosity about Marius's absences. **Théodule's discovery at Vernon**: Théodule encountered Marius kneeling in cemetery upon grave. Marius had strewn bouquet there. At extremity of grave stood cross of black wood with name in white letters: COLONEL BARON PONTMERCY. Marius's sobs were audible. Théodule absolutely put out of countenance by unexpected encounter with sepulchre; experienced singular and disagreeable sensation composed of respect for tomb mingled with respect for colonel. Retreated, leaving Marius alone; Death appeared to him with large epaulets. **Not knowing what to write to aunt about this discovery, Théodule decided not to write at all**; it is probable nothing would have resulted if scene at Vernon had not had almost immediate counter-shock at Paris.

## Political and Social Context (Autumn Year 3)

**Revolutionary ferment**: At that epoch, a certain revolutionary quiver vaguely current. Breaths from depths of '89 and '93 in the air. Youth on point of moulting. People undergoing transformation almost without being conscious of it through movement of age. Needle which moves round compass also moves in souls. Each person taking that step in advance which he was bound to take. Royalists becoming liberals, liberals turning democrats. Flood tide complicated with thousand ebb movements. Opinions traverse phases. Voltairian royalism had no less singular sequel: Bonapartist liberalism.

**Revolutionary organizations**: No vast underlying organizations like German _tugendbund_ and Italian Carbonarism yet existed in France, but here and there dark underminings in process of throwing off shoots. The Cougourde being outlined at Aix; at Paris existed society of the Friends of the A B C among other affiliations. They declared themselves Friends of the A B C—the _Abaissé_,—the debased—that is to say, the people. They wished to elevate the people. They were not numerous, secret society in state of embryo, almost a coterie, if coteries ended in heroes.

**Meeting places**: Assembled in Paris in two localities: near fish-market in wine-shop called _Corinthe_, and near Pantheon in little café in Rue Saint-Michel called _Café Musain_ (now torn down). First meeting-place close to workingman, second to students. Hall tolerably remote from café, connected by extremely long corridor, had two windows and exit with private stairway on little Rue des Grès. They smoked and drank, gambled and laughed, conversed in very loud tones about everything, whispered of other things. Old map of France under the Republic nailed to wall—sign sufficient to excite suspicion of police agent.

**Principal members**: Enjolras, Combeferre, Jean Prouvaire, Feuilly, Courfeyrac, Bahorel, Lesgle or Laigle, Joly, Grantaire. Remarkable group; vanished in invisible depths. Most were students cordial terms with working classes.

**Courfeyrac**: Had father called M. de Courfeyrac. False idea of bourgeoisie under Restoration regarding aristocracy and nobility: belief in particle. Courfeyrac had not wished to remain behind rest, called himself plain Courfeyrac. Wit transmitted from generation to generation of successive levies of youth traversing schools, almost always exactly same; anyone listening to Courfeyrac in 1828 would have thought he heard Tholomyès in 1817. But Courfeyrac honorable fellow. Beneath apparent similarities of exterior mind, difference between him and Tholomyès very great. Latent man in two totally different. District attorney in Tholomyès, paladin in Courfeyrac.

**Lesgle**: King frowned, glanced at signature of petition, beheld name written thus: LESGLE. This non-Bonaparte orthography touched King and he began to smile. Lesgle's ancestor keeper of hounds surnamed Lesgueules; this surname furnished name. Called Lesgueules, by contraction Lesgle, by corruption l'Aigle. King smiled broadly. Later gave man posting office of Meaux, either intentionally or accidentally. Persecutions of fate rendered him inventive; full of resources. Had no money but found means, when it seemed good, to indulge in "unbridled extravagance." One night went so far as to eat "hundred francs" in supper with wench, inspired him to make memorable remark: "Pull off my boots, you five-louis jade."
